source.title: CR-SAM: Curvature Regularized Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Tao Wu; Tie Luo; Donald C. Wunsch

record.tranche_reason: Tests a new curvature measure and a curvature-regularized training method against held-out classification performance, using different measures and interventions from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CR-SAM test accuracy against SGD, SAM, and R-SAM, and reports training/test curvature measurements. It does not test the random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example claims as stated in V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization rationale to develop CR-SAM and evaluates its accuracy and geometry. It tests none of V1–V8. In particular, gradient-normalized Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure, and the study does not evaluate its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that normalized Hessian trace better characterizes curvature and that CR-SAM improves classification performance over the tested baselines. Clarify that ImageNet ViTs use AdamW, while ResNets use SGD with momentum; the study does not show ViT superiority over SGD. These are authors' interpretations, not a test of V7.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces curvature regularization into SAM; compares CR-SAM with SGD, SAM, and R-SAM. It does not use the original methods specified by V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, and data augmentation conditions vary; CR-SAM reports higher test accuracy than SAM in the tabulated CIFAR and ImageNet settings. ImageNet-C and ImageNet-R are out-of-distribution evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: CR-SAM has higher reported accuracy than SAM in all 36 tabulated model, dataset, and augmentation conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding the proposed curvature regularizer to SAM improves image-classification accuracy in these tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100, test-set normalized Hessian trace is 884.95 for CR-SAM, 1193.87 for SAM, and 1674.89 for SGD, alongside increasing test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CR-SAM produces lower gradient-normalized Hessian trace and higher test accuracy than the tested SGD and SAM recipes in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: During SAM training, one-step ascent becomes a poorer approximation to 20-step ascent; normalized Hessian trace grows and shows consistent training/test trends.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-normalized Hessian trace tracks the reported deterioration of SAM's one-step approximation on ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10/100.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy rather than training–test error gaps for its main comparisons. ImageNet table entries provide no uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. Curvature analysis is limited to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 for the geometry table, and the AR reference uses a 20-step ascent approximation rather than an exact optimum.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported CR-SAM-versus-SGD rows were added for the 36 CIFAR and ImageNet settings; those SGD comparator values are noted in the corresponding CR-SAM rows. Figure 4 provides qualitative loss-landscape plots without a numerical measure and is not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Controlled adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons and their dependence on tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, small-data failures, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. For r01–r36, cannot_determine refers to the supplied claim versions, not to whether the reported accuracy improvement exists. CIFAR hyperparameters were selected for highest test accuracy, so these results do not provide an untouched held-out estimate after tuning. Figure 5 includes training/test curves, but these alone do not supply the magnitude-aware sharpness comparison required by V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their test-error effects.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.

The paper measures normalized Hessian trace and its relation to the one-step approximation ratio, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness against training–test gaps or compare it with the specified norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
